key_insight: A combined CEL simulation and ANN model can accurately predict and optimize friction stir welding quality in HDPE by linking process settings to temperature, axial force, and defect formation.
engineering_relevance: The study gives practical welding guidelines for robust thermoplastic joints, showing that bottom preheating and tuned speed settings can reduce defects and stabilize force and thermal fields.
method: 3D coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of HDPE friction stir welding
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental temperature and axial-force data
Validation against experiments and process-map generation for defect-free windows
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved R2 values between 0.91 and 0.99, and the CEL model matched experimental void formation and thermal-mechanical responses well.
watch_item: The model is calibrated to the tested HDPE parameter range, so predictions outside the validated rotational speed, welding speed, and preheating conditions may be unreliable.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
